title: Use a text input
summary: TextInput lets someone type text. onChangeText supplies the new text, so state can keep the field and screen together.
introduction: TextInput lets someone type text. onChangeText supplies the new text, so state can keep the field and screen together. Your task: Type a name and then clear it.
learningObjectives: Type a name and then clear it.

blocks.text: TextInput lets someone type text. onChangeText supplies the new text, so state can keep the field and screen together.
Use a current Expo project with React Native. Put examples in App.jsx. Run the project with Expo on a supported device or emulator. Native components do not run in this website's HTML playground.

blocks.code:
import {useState} from "react";import {View,Text,TextInput} from "react-native";
export default function App(){const [name,setName]=useState("");return <View style={{padding:24}}><Text>Your name</Text><TextInput accessibilityLabel="Your name" value={name} onChangeText={setName} style={{borderWidth:1,padding:12}}/><Text>Hello, {name}</Text></View>;}
blocks.title: Use a text input

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `TextInput` is a native text field. Its `onChangeText` callback receives the new text directly.
`useState` gives React a remembered value and a setter. Call the setter to ask React to show the next value.

blocks.text: The greeting changes as a name is typed.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Keep a visible label and an accessible name. A placeholder alone is not a lasting label.

blocks.text: Type a name and then clear it.
